We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Serve as a contact for SBK processes, procedures, practices, manuals, guidance documents and safety plans and provide guidance to others related to SBK administrative procedures associated with document compliance. Collaborate with subject matter experts to initiate, develop, review, revise, implement and evaluate documentation that impact SBK facilities and systems, as well as LLNL programs. Monitor document tracking and routing, and ensure revision control using electronic applications (e.g., Enterprise Lifecycle Management-Unclassified [ELM-U]/Windchill) for configuration management of documents. Assist in planning, coordinating, and conducting periodic assessments to determine conformance with regulations, LLNL requirements, and SBK plans and procedures, including management self-assessments, observations and inspections, relating to SBK processes and other operational activities; recommend and coordinate completion of corrective action plans related to deficiencies. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. Pay Range $94,560 - $138,888 Annually $94,560 - $115,728 Annually for the A23.2 level $113,400 - $138,888 Annually for the A23.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

The Toxins group within the Product Development, Science & Technology (PDS&T) - Biologics organization supports manufacturing, process validation, regulatory submission, and continuous improvement for late-stage and commercial manufacturing of biological toxin products at AbbVie. We have an exciting opportunity for a Scientist I position based in Irvine, CA. This role involves leveraging scientific and bioengineering principles to develop bioassays for analytical testing at drug substance and drug product release and stability time points. The candidate must possess in-depth knowledge and hands-on experience in a range of techniques, including but not limited to molecular cloning, mammalian cell culture, PCR, Western blot, protein expression, purification, bioassay, transfection, and laboratory automation platforms. Moreover, excellent communication skills and the ability to thrive in a multi-disciplinary and cross-functional team environment are essential for success in this role. Key responsibilities include: Develop, program, operate, and troubleshoot robotic automation platforms, including Hamilton STAR liquid handlers and Opentrons, to support high-throughput screening and testing. Lead scientific initiatives by generating innovative technical ideas and strategic approaches to advance research goals and address experimental challenges. Demonstrate strong scientific judgment by aligning research activities with project objectives and adapting experimental plans based on new data, evolving priorities, and project developments. Design, execute, and interpret complex experiments using rigorous, reproducible methodologies. Develop, optimize, and implement novel experimental protocols by leveraging emerging technologies to advance scientific progress and resolve technical issues. Maintain current expertise in relevant scientific and technical disciplines and apply best practices from current literature to experimental design, troubleshooting, and method development. Establish and manage experimental timelines, track progress closely, and ensure timely delivery of project milestones through strong organization and time-management. Draft, review, and edit SOPs, technical reports, publications, presentations, and patent applications in accordance with industry and regulatory standards. Communicate scientific concepts, experimental data, and key findings effectively to cross-functional teams and stakeholders through clear written and oral presentations. Bachelor’s degree, or equivalent education, with typically 5 years of relevant experience; or Master’s degree, or equivalent education, with typically 2 years of relevant experience in Cell and Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biochemical or Biomedical Engineering, Biotechnology, or a closely related discipline. Hands-on experience with scripting and programming robotic liquid handlers (e.g., Hamilton STAR and Opentrons) and proficiency in software platforms like VENUS and Python. Experience translating manual cell-based assays, including ELISA and potency assays, into automated workflows. Practical experience with molecular cloning, mammalian cell culture, PCR, Western blotting, bioassays, and transfection procedures. Knowledgeable in genome editing approaches, including CRISPR/Cas9, with a solid understanding of experimental design, execution, and validation of gene-editing studies. Experience in optimizing and qualifying cell-based potency assays, including sample testing. Strong computer skills essential for scientific research, including word processing, spreadsheets, presentation software, and advanced data analysis. Ability to analyze, interpret, and present complex datasets using scientific software such as Python, R, and JMP. Previous GxP experience and attention to detail in documentation preferred. Demonstrated ability to design experiments, solve problems creatively, develop comprehensive experimental plans, and independently troubleshoot and validate results. Ability to stay current with scientific advances, critically evaluate relevant literature, and rapidly incorporate new concepts and techniques into research activities. Detail-oriented, with a proven ability to generate high-quality, reproducible data within tight deadlines. Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary, cross-functional teams and communicate complex scientific concepts clearly in both verbal and written formats. Self-motivated, adaptable, and committed to scientific discovery, continuous learning, and process improvement. Experience developing and optimizing these models for research or drug discovery applications is highly desirable.

Experience working with teams developing and deploying high quality software products; specifically, gathering requirements, implementing software, debugging and remediating issues, coupled with prior coding and/or automation experience. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. The Associate Director provides statistical programming support for multiple clinical projects across multiple therapeutic areas, both through individual contribution and through the work of staff. The Associate Director provides training and performance management for staff. The Associate Director demonstrates leadership competencies, builds relationships, and promotes teamwork within the Statistical Programming organization and across functions. The Associate Director is accountable for ensuring statistical programming support is delivered across multiple therapeutic areas. The Associate Director makes key recommendations and decisions related to processes, standards, and resource management. The Associate Director is also responsible for staff management and development. Responsibilities: SAS Programming: Demonstrates a strong understanding of SAS programming concepts and techniques used in the pharmaceutical industry and applies that knowledge to resolve non-routine problems. Standards: Oversees the development and implementation of global company standards for output design and programming conventions and monitors regulatory guidance and industry best practices. CRFs and Database Definitions: Provides strategic guidance on CRF and database design and reviews global standards related to these deliverables. Derivation Programming, Submission Data Sets, and Programs: Interprets statistical analysis plans, develops analysis data set specifications, and oversees the development and implementation of global standards for derived data sets and submission programs. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Works collaboratively with stakeholders to manage priorities and resources across therapeutic areas. Demonstrates a solid understanding of drug development principles, anticipates risks, develops contingency and escalation plans, and contributes to cross-functional initiatives. Communication: Presents statistical programming concepts, risk assessments, and recommendations clearly and persuasively to statisticians, scientists, programmers, and non-scientists. Effectively leads meetings and presentations. Training and Mentoring: Provides guidance, training, and mentoring to staff to support development and ensure compliance with training requirements. Staff Management : Assigns responsibilities, defines scope, and reviews progress to ensure projects are delivered on time and with appropriate quality. Allocates resources to maintain the right balance of expertise across projects and collaborates with management to assess staffing needs. Sets high expectations, promotes open communication, and leads staff to meet organizational goals. Provides performance management for 4–10 statistical programmers. Minimum Qualifications: Degree in Statistics, Computer Science, or a related field 10+ years of statistical programming experience (with MS) OR 12+ years of statistical programming experience (with BS) Strong technical competence in SAS programming and macro development. Experience in pharmaceutical clinical trials. Experience with regulatory filings such as NDA, BLA, or other submissions, including ISS and ISE experience. Preferred Qualifications: Experience interacting with regulatory agencies, especially FDA and EMEA. Previous management experience. Other Required Skills: Working knowledge of ICH guidelines and relevant regulatory requirements. Strong oral and written communication skills.

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

At Visa, AI is central to our vision for the future of payments and commerce. Evaluate emerging AI/ML techniques, benchmark performance, and validate business impact using real Visa datasets and use cases. Support the end-to-end delivery of AI COE projects, including: Identifying and refining problem statements with stakeholders Prototyping advanced models, pipelines, and automation workflows Building high-quality, reusable code assets Ensuring production readiness and integration with enterprise systems Develop technical documentation, metadata, and best practices for validated AI methods. Contribute to quality assurance through code reviews, prompt engineering support, model evaluation frameworks, and benchmark design. Ensure compliance with governance, security, and Responsible AI standards in all AI COE outputs. Quantify and communicate impact using KPIs such as model accuracy, workflow efficiency gains, adoption metrics, and business value delivered. Collaborate with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and global partners to embed AI COE solutions into enterprise workflows and maximize adoption. AbbVie’s Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function is seeking a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Associate Director to provide analytics leadership for the Business Evolution Strategic Development (BESD) Team. Communicate complex findings and insight-driven narratives to senior leadership and cross-functional teams, enabling improved payer knowledge and strategic decision-making. Monitor external environment and translate emerging trends (political, regulatory, legislative, commercial) into strategic recommendations for AbbVie’s business evolution. Advise on analytics infrastructure enhancements to drive business impact. Leadership and Influence: Influence and persuade across multiple external and internal stakeholders. Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with internal stakeholders, external market experts and partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree (MBA or related business/science) preferred. 10+ years of progressive analytical/ insights experience in healthcare industry (pharma, consulting, government affairs, market access, public policy, etc.). 1-2 years pharmaceutical market access experience with deep understanding of Health Plans, PBMs, Hospitals, Specialty Pharmacies, and healthcare policy stakeholders. Strong insurance channel experience and understanding (i.e. Medicare, Commercial etc.) Strong business acumen, strategic and analytical thinking, and executive presence. Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to distill complex information into compelling, concise messages. Strong organizational skills, flexibility, attention to detail, and experience in collaborative, dynamic environments. Exceptional communications and executive presence, critical thinking and interpersonal skills, strong ability to influence without authority, the ability to speak and write persuasively and with clarity, strong organizational skills, flexibility, and adaptability to changing requirements, resourcefulness and creativity, strong attention to detail, a proven track record of being able to work drive towards deadlines and an ability to work collaboratively in a fluid organizational and external environment. Must be an individual who works well in a team environment and enjoys working in a collegial, collaborative and fun, yet highly demanding culture Preferred: Experience in policy shaping, price reform strategy, and enterprise-level stakeholder partnership. Proficiency with pharmaceutical data sources (formulary, claims).

We have an opening for a NEST Readiness Coordinator to oversee and execute LLNL’s Nuclear Emergency Support Team (NEST) responder readiness program. This role requires familiarity with DOE Order 153.1 and LLNL’s compliance with these requirements. You will administer and maintain readiness and training records, execute routine readiness checks and notifications using established procedures, and prepare recurring reports for program customers and management. Additional key aspects of the program include coordination of the on-call watchbill schedule, determining which qualified responders are assigned to on-call periods based on established eligibility and coverage requirements, and verifying required training and readiness items are current prior to assignment. The position coordinates updates across institutional systems and stakeholders, resolves routine issues by interpreting applicable guidelines, and escalates discrepancies that could impact readiness or on-call coverage. This position will be in the NEST Program Element within the Global Security Principal Directorate’s Nuclear Threat Reduction (N) Program. In this role, you will Participates in the development, maintenance, and improvement of the NEST responder readiness database and associated tools. Partner with the Readiness Program Lead, assess and analyze established readiness support processes and workflows, ensuring tasks are completed accurately and on time. Respond to customer questions and resolve routine readiness administration issues by interpreting and explaining procedures, guidelines, and manuals. Maintain, review data, and summarize results to support resolution of readiness discrepancies. Maintain service area records, databases, and documentation for responder readiness and training tracking. Collect, validate, reconcile, compile, and report readiness information across systems, such as, ARMS, TRAKEN, WCD, and related tools. Prepare routine and standard reports for customer use and management decision-making, including completion status, discrepancy tracking, and readiness summaries. Monitor routine readiness checks, notifications, and follow-ups; track completion and document exceptions. Maintain an escalation contact list/tree for routing readiness issues to the appropriate points of contact. Build, publish, and maintain the LLNL Master NEST on-call watch and deployment roster, determining on-call assignments using established coverage rules, qualification criteria, and availability inputs from Deployment POCs and responder organizations. Maintain documentation of responder requirements (on-call expectations, baseline training, gear and communications requirements as applicable), updating content per established guidance. Support upkeep of the NEST Deskbook by performing updates, maintaining version control, and routing edits for review/approval per defined process. Maintain a database used to document NEST facility capabilities, resources, and configurations. Coordinate onboarding/offboarding administrative steps for contractor and subcontractor personnel that support NEST readiness, such as, access requests, account tracking, required documentation, and following established procedures. Track issuance and inventory records for communications devices, such as,pagers, cell phones, Starlink units, and coordinate updates with supporting organizations. Support tracking of vendor/contract readiness-related information by maintaining records and reporting actions to the appropriate contract or technical points of contact. Perform other duties as assigned. This position requires an Active DOE Q clearance (or active Top-Secret clearance) with ability to obtain Sensitive Compartmented Information access. Experience coordinating responder readiness activities, workflow, and processes in- service operations, customer service, operations support, logistics, or mission support environment. Ability to maintain accurate records, databases, and documentation using tools such as SharePoint lists/libraries, spreadsheets, or similar systems. Experience in collecting, validating, and reporting operational data with attention to detail and data integrity. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to document processes and requirements clearly and explain procedures to customers. Experience in tracking and coordinating multiple, parallel tasks and following through discrepancies to closure. Experience working collaboratively with cross-functional teams and multiple stakeholders. Must have a valid California driver’s license. The Center for Global Security Research (CGSR) was established at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) in 1996 to bring together experts from the science, technology, and policy communities to address pressing national security challenges. For over 20 years, CGSR has engaged diverse perspectives on topics important to national security, deterrence, diplomacy, dual-use technology, arms control, nonproliferation, space, cyber, biosecurity, and energy security. We have openings in Fall 2026 for undergraduate students to engage in practical research on global security topics. Students will work with CGSR over the duration of three to four months as a research associate (RA). RAs will engage in practical research to further their educational and career goals, while also supporting the development of strategies for national security and LLNL’s mission focus areas. Examples of relevant fields of research include nuclear deterrence, arms control, nonproliferation, emerging technologies, cybersecurity, space, biological & chemical security, and energy security. CGSR’s objectives are as follows: To explore the dynamics of potential 21st century strategic conflicts (i.e., those with a potential nuclear aspect) and to formulate ideas about how to achieve U.S. deterrence and other objectives in such conflicts. To explore the sources and characteristics of strategic competition in the emerging security environment and to formulate organizing concepts to enhance the competitive position of the United States and its allies and partners over the long term. To identify whether and how technically based approaches can address new challenges to national and international security. To catalyze broader national and international thinking about the requirements of effective deterrence, assurance, and strategic stability in a changed and changing security environment. To assist in the development of new generations of experts motivated by a clear view of the changed and changing security environment. More information on CGSR, its research focus areas, and its publications can be found at https://cgsr.llnl.gov/ . This job will be closed to applicants on May 31, 2026. You will Conduct an independent research project on an agreed upon topic aligned with CGSR/LLNL research priorities under the supervision of CGSR staff. Support CGSR/LLNL through contributions to ongoing research activities. Tasks may include contributing to literature reviews, annotated bibliographies, and workshop summary reports. Attend relevant research seminars, speakers’ series, and workshops. Present research to LLNL staff at end of the assignment. Prepare end-of-assignment technical report or publication. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112 of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). See Additional Information section below for details. Must be currently enrolled in an accredited university or have completed AA/AS degree in a field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Areas of study include international relations and/or security, political science, economics, public policy, emerging technologies, nonproliferation, energy, biosecurity, foreign language studies, or related fields. Demonstrated academic and/or professional achievement in a relevant field of research aligned with CGSR analytic priorities. Strong record of independent research and publication, or a strong proposal of research to be done while at CGSR and in future academic and professional settings. Ability to work in a team environment. Pay Range $23.26 - $31.62 Hourly This position is under a step structure. Please note that the step is determined by your academic level. Transcripts are required.

The Producer must be able to manage multiple assignments simultaneously, adapt quickly to breaking news, and collaborate closely with editorial leadership and production teams. The ideal candidate has experience working in a multiplatform newsroom and demonstrates strong knowledge of social media and digital storytelling. This role requires strong editorial judgment, the ability to work under tight deadlines, and a solid understanding of national and international news, including breaking news coverage. Responsibilities include requesting graphics and other visual elements that support storytelling and enhance the presentation of stories across platforms. The Multimedia Producer may also assist in writing scripts and editorial content for newscasts and digital coverage. This position requires a strong visual sense and the ability to identify compelling video, natural sound, and other elements that strengthen the narrative and overall impact of a story. In addition, the Multiplatform Producer is responsible for booking guests on a daily basis for linear, streaming, and digital platforms. The candidate must be able to work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute. The position requires the ability to work flexible hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays, particularly during breaking news coverage or special assignments. This position demands the ability to work effectively under tight deadlines within a fast-paced and evolving newsroom environment. Responsibilities: • Gather editorial elements needed for stories, including social media newsgathering, research, and securing interviews. • Contribute to the day’s editorial direction by pitching story ideas, exclusive reports, and interview opportunities. • Participate in breaking news coverage and special projects. • Demonstrate proficiency in using social media platforms for newsgathering, research, and content creation. • Maintain a well-established network of contacts, including community organizations, business leaders, federal and local officials, and other media outlets. • Work effectively in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment, including weekends, early mornings, and flexible hours to accommodate last-minute scheduling changes. • Operate under the guidance of the VP of News Gathering • This position is based on-site in Miami, Florida, and requires regular in-office presence to support newsroom operations. • Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and accountable newsroom culture. Basic Requirements: Bachelor’s degree in journalism, Communications, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum of 3 years of on-air news reporting experience in Spanish. Experience producing digital video content in a newsroom environment is a plus. Proficiency in social media platforms and trends. Fluent in Spanish, written and spoken. Fluent in English Desired Characteristics: Accustomed to working in a team and collaborating with all levels within the organization. Proven excellent interpersonal skills combined with a strong sense of how to visually tell a compelling story. Outside of the box thinker Proficient in I-News, helpful Additional Requirements: Interested candidate must submit a resume/CV through www.nbcunicareers.com to be considered (job #: ) Must be willing to work in the greater Miami, Florida area. Must be 18 years or older. Must have a valid driver’s license. Must have unrestricted work authorization to work in the United States Must be covered by Solutions, NBCU’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Program

The Real-Time Graphics Specialist is responsible for the design, development, deployment, and optimization of high-quality real-time broadcast graphics for live studio and event productions. This role blends advanced creative execution with strong technical expertise to support dynamic, on-air visual storytelling. The Specialist manages the graphics production lifecycle — from concept through live delivery — while collaborating closely with producers, directors, and technical teams. This position plays a key role in maintaining broadcast standards, improving workflows, troubleshooting live graphics issues, and contributing to innovation in augmented reality (AR), virtual reality production VR, and data-driven graphics. This is a hands-on role requiring creativity, precision, technical depth, and the ability to perform under live broadcast deadlines. Key Responsibilities 1. Graphics Design & Development Create and customize templates and animations for live broadcasts, including lower thirds, over-the-shoulder graphics, data visualizations, touchscreen graphics, and virtual/augmented reality elements Develop and deploy graphics using real-time rendering engines such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or HTML-based systems Plan, build, maintain, and update graphic directories and playout systems for studio and event workflows Translate creative direction into compelling design, animation, and layout solutions Optimize graphics for performance, stability, and compliance with broadcast standards Prepare and manage image files and assets for production use Ensure visual consistency and adherence to brand standards 2. Workflow Management & Process Optimization Manage the full graphics production pipeline from concept to on-air execution Organize and maintain a centralized graphics asset library with proper version control and archiving Establish, document, and improve efficient workflows and best practices Track and report on project deliverables and performance metrics Assist with hardware/software upgrades and studio builds 3. Collaboration & Live Production Support Collaborate with producers, directors, show teams, and technical staff to meet project goals Serve as a primary contact for troubleshooting real-time graphics issues during live broadcasts Support graphics playout in live event and studio environments Work closely with production teams to design graphics tailored to specific programs or segments Communicate clearly with to manage expectations and ensure timely delivery Independently research and resolve technical challenges 4. Innovation & Industry Advancement Stay current with emerging technologies in real-time graphics and broadcast production Explore opportunities in AR, VR, virtual studios, and data-driven storytelling Contribute innovative ideas that elevate production value and visual storytelling Continuously expand technical skillsets and share knowledge with peers Basic Qualifications Minimum 5+ years of professional experience in real-time television graphics with a strong portfolio/demo reel Advanced expertise in platforms such as Vizrt, Unreal Engine, Zero Density, Flowics, or similar systems Strong understanding of broadcast standards, live production workflows, and playout systems Advanced 2D and 3D animation skills with strong typography and layout abilities Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills under live broadcast pressure Strong organizational and communication skills Ability to work flexible hours in live production environments Desired Characteristics: 8+ years of live broadcast graphics experience Familiarity with AR/VR workflows and virtual production tools Knowledge of 3D modeling and animation tools such as Cinema 4D, Blender, or Maya Experience implementing hardware/software upgrades or new studio builds Education Required: High School Diploma or equivalent Preferred: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in design, animation, broadcast technology, or related field Work Environment In-office requirement: four days per week Must be able to work flexible schedules, including evenings and weekends

In this internship, you will conduct advanced research and engineering in 3D perception, scene understanding, and machine learning to address challenges in autonomous systems. Integrate the resulting system/software into existing Bosch platform. Summarize research findings in high-quality paper and/or patent submissions. Position Purpose: Installs and repairs all electrical work throughout the treatment distribution system. Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first). Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role. If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies. For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months. The ST role is an at-will position, meaning that the Company or ST can terminate the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason at all, with or without cause. Under general supervision, the Seal Repair Technician is responsible for all processes related to disassembly and assembly of rotating equipment. The Seal Repair Technician follows instruction from a Repair job packet and router to perform DCI (Dismantle Clean and Inspect) and gives a written description of the wear and condition of critical components seal. This position completes all inspection forms taking pictures of all critical components and uses inspection equipment for proper documentation of the assembly. With assistance identifies, inspects and evaluates material returned, determines repair operations, performs simple shop operations, verify specifications, initiate work and purchase orders. Receives John Crane parts and materials returned by customers and branch offices. Ensures all components are properly cleaned and free from foreign material per departmental procedures Performs the assembly of the seal once the repair has been released to the shop and all components have been replaced or reconditioned and marked ready for assembly. May perform parts structuring, checks cost structure, and determines price of repair, ensures assembly is structured correctly, and price repair. Determines necessary repair operations, ensures BOM (bill of materials) / drawings / repair parts match. Performs simple operations on drill press (single spindle), tool post grinder, bead blast polisher and lapping machine. Verifies part specifications with measuring instruments such as micrometer, vernier caliper, dial indicator and optical flats. May initiates purchase orders for new jobs if vendors are involved. Consults with Engineering or Sales departments as necessary. Maintains necessary records and small inventory of seal parts used for repair orders. Works from factory work orders, prints, rework orders and verbal instructions. Assists newer repair personnel as necessary. Sets up and troubleshoots lapping machines for repair maintenance. May perform direct contact with customers on service and/or phone, checks computer system for credit and address information, price repairs. High School diploma or equivalent. 1-2 years' experience in mechanical assembly positions. Experience with mechanical seals is a plus.

THE POSITION: Medical Information is a critically important customer-facing function that supports the safe and effective use of pharmaceutical company products by providing timely, scientifically balanced, evidence based, nonpromotional information in response to unsolicited requests from healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and payers. Medical Information also plays an important role in post-marketing handling of adverse events and product complaints. As part of the Medical Information Contact Center (MICC) team, this position delivers industry-leading services, which include Contact Center staffing for responding to product information requests, identifying and handling of adverse events and/or product quality issues, and medical writing as needed to generate written response for use in response to medical questions received. This position requires clinical and therapeutic knowledge, critical and analytical thinking, and customer/patient-centric approach. Medical Information Specialists typically support multiple pharmaceutical clients, multiple products, and multiple therapeutic areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by: MEDICAL INFORMATION SUPPORT Respond to medical information inquiries from physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other health care professionals, consumers, and payers. Utilize medical information skills to identify, research, and critically evaluate medical literature to create responses to medical information inquiries. Utilize writing skills for adverse event and product complaint narrative during intake as well as medical inquiry custom responses. Handle requests across multiple channels and platforms (phone, email, CRM, chat, etc.) Identify adverse events and product complaints during interactions with customers. Perform intake sufficient to generate adverse event and product complaint reports in compliance with EVERSANA-MICC and client standard operating procedures. Knowledge of FDA’s postmarketing adverse event reporting regulations and safety terminology. Ability to make accurate assessments regarding what information needs to be obtained and level or depth of information to be collected. Coordinate processes necessary for responding to product quality-related complaints. This process may involve interactions with personnel in the following departments: Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and the complainant. Maintain product, therapeutic area, and client specific requirements knowledge. Ensure good documentation, high quality, and excellent customer service. Medical writing and Medical Information content development. Provide medical writing to assist in drafting of Medical Information response documents [FAQs, Scientific Response Documents (SRDs), Custom Response Documents (CRDs)] and/or work collaboratively with medical writing team to develop these materials.  Staffing at scientific medical affairs booths. On-call responsibilities on an as assigned basis. Miscellaneous projects such as market and competitive product research, operational and process improvements, field team training and field liaison support.  All other duties as assigned. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. Customer Services: Maintain and improve customer services associated with activity of the Medical Communications Contact Center. Hours: Able to work full time and be flexible with work scheduling as required by clients and management. Travel: In general, this position does not travel; however, the incumbent will need to be able to travel up to 10%. We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. We are looking for a Counterintelligence Officer in the Counterintelligence Program to perform comprehensive research and analysis, conduct interviews, and present recommendations to senior management, high-level DOE personnel, and officials of intelligence agencies on relevant counterintelligence (CI) issues, ensuring the Laboratory’s compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) Order 475.1 (CI Program). Job Description At BioLife, we know that flexibility matters—especially for those balancing multiple commitments. That's why we're dedicated to creating meaningful part-time opportunities for our team. This role is truly part-time , with most shifts lasting between 4 to 6 hours a day, 3+ days per week —designed to fit your life. • We’ll confirm your availability and shift days and times early in the interview process. And, because we value open communication, you’ll always be informed about any schedule changes in advance. • Our patients depend on the plasma we collect, so your reliability during your scheduled hours is greatly valued. However, our part-time roles are designed with the understanding that flexibility on both sides is key. Whether you’re looking for extra income, a way to gain valuable experience, or a schedule that fits your busy life—BioLife welcomes part-time team members just like you! Start strong with our paid, interactive training program! Please take this virtual tour to get a sneak peek of one of our Plasma Donation Centers. About the role: Every day, the donors you meet will motivate you. The high-quality plasma you collect will become life-changing medicines. Here, a commitment to customer service and quality is expected. You will report to the Plasma Center Manager and will perform as a plasma donor screener and perform phlebotomy to support plasma center operations. How you will contribute: · You will answer phones, and greet and focus on our donors, while ensuring the safety of donors and our team. · You will screen new and repeat donors and take and record donor vital signs and finger stick results. · You will use our Donor Information System, prepare donor charts, maintain accurate records, and coordinate donor compensation. · You will help identify operational opportunities for continuous improvement and initiate changes to center processes using company approved procedures. · You will be there for our donors, which includes working a variety of shifts, Saturdays and Sundays, and holidays. What you bring to Takeda: · High school diploma or equivalent · Ability to walk and/or stand for the entire work shift · Will work evenings, weekends, and holidays · Ability to lean, bend, stoop, crouch, and reach above shoulders and below knees · Ability to lift to 5 lbs., and occasional lifting of materials up to 32 lbs. and rarely 50 lbs. · Fine motor coordination, depth perception, and ability to hear equipment from a distance · Because of potential exposure to bloodborne pathogens (risk level 1), 90% of work tasks require prolonged glove wear · 1 or more years minimum experience working in a customer or patient facing role is helpful What Takeda can offer you: Every day at Takeda, we feel good knowing that what we do helps improve the lives of patients with rare diseases. At BioLife, while you focus on our donors, we will support you. We offer a purpose you can believe in, a team you can count on, opportunities for career growth, and a comprehensive benefits program to include retirement benefits, medical/dental, family leave, disability insurance and more, all in a fast-paced, friendly environment. More about us: At Takeda, we are transforming patient care through the development of novel specialty pharmaceuticals and best in class patient support programs. Takeda is a patient-focused company that will inspire and empower you to grow through life-changing work. Certified as a Global Top Employer, Takeda offers stimulating careers, encourages innovation, and strives for excellence in everything we do. We foster an inclusive, collaborative workplace, in which our teams are united by an unwavering commitment to provide Better Health and a Brighter Future to people around the world. Success in this position demands rapid decision-making, effective communication, and proactive collaboration with cross-functional teams to minimize business impact during disruptions. Weekend shift availability is mandatory, as the role includes working on weekends as part of the regular schedule. What you will be responsible for Major Incident Management Provide strategic oversight of critical IT disruptions. Drive rapid service restoration and minimize client impact. Prioritize reduction of Mean Time to Restore Service (MTRS) to uphold operational resilience. 24/7 Technical Bridge – Non-Major Incident Resolution Lead continuous global support for lower-tier IT issues. Enable proactive resolution through real-time coordination and cross-functional engagement. Enhance system stability and reduce recurrence of incidents. Daily Operational Health Check Conduct structured tri-daily reviews (Mon–Fri) with Application and Infrastructure teams. Assess system health, identify emerging risks, and ensure operational readiness across the enterprise. Event & Hypercare Management Govern high-impact IT events end-to-end, including milestone tracking and escalation protocols. Monitor real-time performance during critical periods to ensure seamless execution and stability. Maintain integrated communication channels for effective stakeholder engagement. Weekend Change Governance Oversee weekend deployments with a focus on risk mitigation and operational stability. Provide structured governance and coordination to safeguard service integrity during high-change windows. What we value These skills will help you succeed in this role: Breadth of knowledge across infrastructure and application processes, areas, and technologies (Network, Security, Open Systems, Mainframe, Storage, Database, Middleware, Cloud, End User Computing, and Application) Ability and aptitude to pick up new technologies and procedures Strong communication skills (written, verbal and presentation). Demonstrated ability to succinctly identify and summarize key findings to various stakeholders. Ability to coordinate and communicate across multidisciplinary / multicultural teams across countries and regions Proven analytical and problem-solving skills Strong collaboration skills; ability to listen and understand without interruption and remain calm and composed, especially in stressful situations Good stakeholder management, able to work well under pressure and deal with demanding stakeholders across the business Education & Preferred Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or the equivalent field Strong ITSM knowledge and experience: The resource should have a solid understanding of IT Service Management principles and hands-on experience with ITSM tools and processes. Proven experience managing major incidents in large-scale enterprise environments. Ability to work during weekends as per business needs. Job Description At General Motors, our product teams are redefining mobility. Through a human-centered design process, we create vehicles and experiences that are designed not just to be seen, but to be felt. We’re turning today’s impossible into tomorrow’s standard —from breakthrough hardware and battery systems to intuitive design, intelligent software, and next-generation safety and entertainment features. Every day, our products move millions of people as we aim to make driving safer, smarter, and more connected, shaping the future of transportation on a global scale. ARC Productization Engineer At General Motors, our ARC (Advanced Robotics Center) team is redefining how robotics enable safer, more flexible, and more efficient manufacturing. We are developing and deploying next‑generation robotic solutions that move materials, automate complex tasks, and unlock new levels of throughput and quality in our plants. The ARC Productization Engineer serves as the critical link between ARC Product Development and downstream Product Execution and Deployment teams. In this role, you will ensure that ARC‑developed robotics solutions are manufacturing‑ready , validated for proof‑of‑concept (PoC) testing , and prepared for scalable deployment across GM plants. Working primarily in the plant environment, you will identify and close readiness gaps, drive integration and validation activities, and enable a smooth handoff from development to execution. The Role Acting on behalf of the ARC Product Development organization, the ARC Productization Engineer operates at the intersection of product engineering , manufacturing operations , and deployment . You will: Represent ARC at manufacturing plants, serving as the on‑site technical owner for ARC products during PoC, pilot, and early deployment. Translate plant needs, constraints, and lessons learned into clear requirements and feedback for ARC Product Development. Build and maintain product readiness views that describe what is required to move from prototype to robust, repeatable deployment. This is a highly hands‑on, on‑site role that combines technical depth, structured problem solving, and strong cross‑functional communication. What You’ll Do Independently represent ARC Product Development at GM manufacturing plants to plan and execute ARC product proof‑of‑concept and pilot deployments . Lead product readiness assessments , identifying gaps in: Design maturity and robustness Manufacturability and serviceability Documentation and standard work Safety, compliance, and operating procedures Process readiness in the plant (material flow, layout, staffing, training) Support on‑site integration, validation, and early deployment activities in Flint, MI and/or Spring Hill, TN, including: System bring‑up and functional checkout Integration with plant material flow, safety systems, and IT/OT infrastructure Execution of PoC test plans and data collection Develop clear, structured handoff packages for Product Execution and Deployment teams, including: Readiness status and open issues Operating constraints and known limitations Standard work, operating procedures, and training content Lessons learned and recommendations for next deployments Collaborate cross‑functionally with Product Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Global Supply Chain (GSC), Industrial Engineering, Safety, Quality, Program Management , and plant leadership. Capture lessons learned from plant deployments and systematically feed insights back into ARC Product Development (requirements updates, design changes, validation plans, documentation). Contribute to standardized deployment playbooks for ARC products, enabling plant and regional teams to deploy with predictable outcomes. Key Responsibilities 1. Product Readiness & Validation Assess product readiness from prototype through PoC and early pilot, with clear criteria for: Functional performance in plant conditions Safety and compliance with GM and regulatory requirements Operability, maintainability, and usability for plant teams Support the creation and execution of PoC and pilot validation plans , ensuring they are: Structured to generate actionable learnings (not just demonstrations) Traceable to requirements from ARC Product Development and plant stakeholders Repeatable across multiple plants and product configurations Document findings, risks, and mitigation plans, and track closure with ARC and plant teams. 2. Plant Integration & Deployment Support Plan and coordinate on‑site activities required to deploy ARC products into live manufacturing environments, including: Site readiness reviews (layout, infrastructure, IT/OT, material flow) Installation, commissioning, and integration of ARC systems Interfaces with plant safety systems, material handling, and operations Work hands‑on with plant personnel to stabilize early deployments, debug issues, and align on operational envelopes and constraints. Ensure that ARC products are introduced in a way that minimizes disruption to plant operations while maximizing learning value. 3. Handoff to Execution & Scaling Build and maintain deployment‑ready documentation , including: System overviews and interface definitions Standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work instructions Maintenance and troubleshooting guides Training materials for operators, maintenance, and engineering Define and communicate clear handoff criteria from Product Development to Product Execution and Deployment teams. Support the transition from one‑off PoCs to repeatable deployment playbooks that can be applied across multiple plants and programs. 4. Cross‑Functional Collaboration & Continuous Improvement Serve as the on‑site SME for ARC products, translating between: ARC engineers and plant teams Suppliers and GM stakeholders Safety, Quality, Manufacturing Engineering, and Operations Capture and prioritize continuous improvement opportunities across design, validation, documentation, and deployment processes. Help refine ARC’s manufacturing readiness and launch frameworks based on real‑world experience in GM plants. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Industrial, Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, or related field). 3+ years of experience working in or directly supporting manufacturing plant environments . Working knowledge of Global Supply Chain (GSC), Industrial Engineering, or Manufacturing Engineering processes and how they interact with plant operations. Ability to work on‑site in Flint, MI or Spring Hill, TN to support product readiness, integration, and proof‑of‑concept activities. Strong skills in technical documentation, communication, and cross‑functional collaboration , with the ability to align diverse stakeholders. Demonstrated ability to quickly learn new technology , understand system behavior in the field, and become the subject matter expert (SME) at a deployment site. Proven capability to work independently in a plant environment, manage day‑to‑day priorities, and escalate issues appropriately. What Will Give You a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications) Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI) , pilot programs, or proof‑of‑concept deployments in manufacturing. Background in robotics, automation, or advanced manufacturing systems , especially in production environments. Familiarity with manufacturing readiness, validation, or launch frameworks , including how to define and measure readiness criteria. Experience developing handoff documentation and playbooks between engineering, deployment, and plant operations teams. Hands‑on experience with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) , industrial robots, or similar mechatronic systems. Comfort operating in ambiguous, fast‑moving environments , balancing speed of learning with the rigor needed for safety and quality. Work Location & Travel This role is onsite , with the majority of time spent in GM manufacturing plants: One position will travel frequently to Spring Hill or be based in the Spring Hill, TN area. One position will primarily support Flint Assembly (Flint, MI) . Around 90% of work time is expected to be spent on‑site at assembly plants , with potential travel to both Flint and Spring Hill and occasional travel to other GM sites as needed. GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc). This role is categorized as onsite. This means the selected candidate is expected to report to a specific location on a full-time basis. The selected candidate will be required to travel at least 50% or more on a frequent basis. This job may be eligible for relocation benefits.
