These positions are field based / remote in the following locations: CA, WA, OR, IA, MN, IN, OH, FL. Candidates must reside in one of the these states and be willing to travel for site visits. Purpose Advance AbbVie's pipeline by striving for excellence in clinical research, turning science into medicine for our patients and leveraging new advanced capabilities to drive industry leading performance. Partners with the investigator and site staff for meaningful and effective engagements positioning AbbVie as the choice in clinical trials. Focus on site clinical research that ensures appropriate conduct of the trial while driving improvement in data integrity, compliance, overall study performance and customer experience. Responsibilities Considered as the primary point of contact for the investigative site. High level of competency or experience in providing contextual information on the clinical trials, connects stakeholder to the investigative sites and strengthens AbbVie’s positioning. Aligns, trains and motivates the site staff and principal investigator on the goals of the clinical trial program, protocol and patient treatment principles for the trial ensuring a trusted partnership. Conducts site evaluation, site training, routine, and site closure monitoring activities with compliance to the protocol and monitoring plans, in accordance with applicable regulations, Good Clinical Practices (GCPs), ICH Guidelines, AbbVie Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and quality standards, ensuring safety and protection of study subjects. Advanced understanding of site engagement and ability to customize site engagement strategy for assigned study (ies). Gather local/site insights and utilize site engagement tools such as the Customer Relationship Management (CRM) tool, to report/track progress and measure impact of that strategy. Advanced level of competency connecting the study protocol, scientific principles and clinical trial requirements to the day-to-day clinical trial execution activities. Evaluate and ensure effective recruitment and retention techniques/plans based on the patient disease journey. Develop solid knowledge of therapeutic area, asset and clinical landscape / patient journey to enable successful patient recruitment and overall protocol compliance. Possesses experienced level of competency to mentor and train less experienced CRAs on various aspects of work and provides input into their development. May participate in global/local task forces and initiatives. Responsible for activities as assigned by manager. Responsible for continuous risk-assessment proactively, and in collaboration with Central Monitoring team, monitor activities conducted by clinical sites to detect early overall study performance or patient safety issues. Advanced ability to think critically to resolve site risk signals while having robust understanding of site processes to drive study execution. Ensures preventative and corrective action plans are put into place, as needed, to mitigate risk and promote compliance using a customer centric approach. Identifies, evaluates and recommends new/potential investigators/sites on an on going basis. Potential sites may be identified through networking or internal AbbVie requests to assist in the placement of planned clinical studies with qualified investigators. Ensures quality of data submitted from study sites and assures timely submission of data, including appropriate reporting and follow-up for all safety events by site personnel. Ensures audit and regulatory inspection readiness at assigned clinical site at all times. Manages investigator payments as per executed contract obligations, as applicable. Qualifications Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent degree; health related preferred (e.g. Medical, Scientific, Nursing, Pharmacy). Minimum of 1 year of clinically related experience, of which a period of 6 months is required in clinical research monitoring of investigational drug or device trials. Familiar with risk‐based monitoring approach, onsite and offsite monitoring. Knowledge of appropriate therapeutic area indications is preferred with the ability to understand and apply scientific concepts as they relate to the conduct of clinical trials. Advanced knowledge on existing and emerging local regulatory and legal requirements, ICH/GCP Guidelines and applicable policies. Demonstrate strong cross-functional collaboration skills among internal and external stakeholders. Demonstrate strong planning and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively and efficiently in a dynamic environment with competing projects and deadlines. Advanced ability to leverage technology, tools and resources to provide customer centric support based on the health of the site. Strong interpersonal skills with excellent written, verbal, active listening and presentation skills, with ability to establish and leverage site relationships and trusted partnerships through engagement, motivation, and training. Ability to use functional expertise with appropriate guidance, leverage critical thinking skills and apply good judgement to address clinical site issues. Acts with integrity in accordance with AbbVie code of business conduct and leadership values. Self-motivated individual focused on delivering timely and quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment.

The Mastering Coordinator supports NBCUniversal’s Studio Mastering organization by coordinating mastering and sub-mastering workflows that enable timely, accurate delivery of content across the company’s distribution supply chain. This role translates customer and distribution requirements into executable mastering workflows, identifies appropriate source materials, and partners with internal teams, StudioPost Operations, and external vendors to ensure work is delivered on time, within budget, and in accordance with Studio Mastering technical specifications. Responsibilities: Order Management & Workflow Execution Interpret mastering requests and distribution requirements, translating high-level orders into detailed, executable workflows. Define mastering and sub-mastering approaches based on specifications, delivery formats, timelines, and budget constraints. Serve as a day-to-day point of coordination for assigned mastering work, escalating risks and issues as needed. Prime contact for editorial workflow support, assisting editors and workflow specific to editorial projects and servicing Cross-Functional & Vendor Coordination Partner with StudioPost Operations Project Managers to ensure work is completed on schedule and within approved budgets. Coordinate with third-party service providers to support mastering and sub-mastering execution. Maintain ongoing communication with Studio Mastering leadership regarding job status, priorities, and technical considerations. Asset Research & Source Element Identification Research inventory systems and historical records to determine the most appropriate source elements for each mastering request. Collaborate with Studio Mastering subject-matter experts to leverage knowledge of asset history, specifications, and condition. Contribute to ongoing evaluation and improvement of mastering specifications, workflows, and operational processes. Solid understanding of physical and file-based mastering workflows. Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities. Understanding of feature film and television production and post-production lifecycles. Ability to identify workflow efficiencies and support best-practice implementation. Strong customer service mindset and collaborative communication style. We have an opening for a Cloud Operations Engineer to join our team. In this position, you will be responsible for designing, implementing, and managing cloud solutions that support the National Nuclear Security Administration’s (NNSA) business services and programmatic missions, including scientific research and mission-critical operations. This position is in the Enterprise Infrastructure Services (EIS) Division within the Computing Directorate. You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams to drive innovation, improve scalability, and ensure the secure and efficient utilization of cloud resources for NNSA initiatives. This role supports multiple sites across the country and occasional travel is required to collaborate with stakeholders and partners. This position offers the opportunity to work in a dynamic and highly technical environment, supporting critical infrastructure for enterprise-level applications. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either the SES.2 or SES.3 level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Deploy and manage cloud infrastructure (primarily AWS) in support of scientific, engineering, and business applications. Develop automation scripts and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) solutions for cloud resource provisioning and management. Collaborate with researchers, engineers, and IT staff to migrate workloads and optimize applications for cloud environments. Implement and manage cloud financial operations (FinOps) practices to optimize cloud spending, track usage, and collaborate with stakeholders to ensure cost-effective resource allocation. Monitor cloud performance and usage, and implement solutions for high availability, scalability, and cost efficiency. Ensure compliance with Department of Energy (DOE) and NNSA security policies and federal regulations for cloud operations. Provide technical support, documentation, and training for cloud users across the enterprise. Stay abreast of emerging cloud technologies and recommend adoption of innovative solutions. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the SES.3 Level Develop and implement advanced cloud computing environments that align with customer needs and enterprise system strategies, ensuring optimal performance and scalability. Independently configure and utilize systems and cloud management tools to monitor, maintain, and optimize infrastructure operations effectively. Identify, troubleshoot, and document complex system and network issues to ensure timely resolution and minimize disruptions. Ability to obtain and maintain a US DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. Citizenship. Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of technical education and relevant experience. Broad experience in cloud platform administration and support, with proficiency in technologies such as AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, or hybrid cloud environments. Broad knowledge of cloud infrastructure operations, including resource provisioning, automation, and the use of infrastructure management tools. Proficient understanding of cloud support systems, such as virtual networking, identity and access management, and monitoring solutions. Comprehensive experience with cloud architecture documentation tools, including Visio and other office productivity software. Proficient in managing and troubleshooting cloud-based resources and services, including performance monitoring and incident response. Strong interpersonal, verbal, and written communication skills, with the ability to work independently while effectively collaborating with customers and team members. Additional Qualifications at the SES.3 Level Significant experience managing enterprise cloud environments, including platforms such as AWS, Azure, and hybrid cloud networking. Advanced knowledge of troubleshooting techniques, with strong skills in resolving issues through analysis of logs, metrics, and cloud-native diagnostic tools. Significant experience with resource provisioning, automation, and infrastructure as management tools, such as Terraform, CloudFormation, Cloud Development Kit, or similar platforms. Significant experience training and mentoring team members, focusing on cloud engineering best practices and architectural design principles. Desired Qualifications Active Department of Energy (DOE) Q-level clearance or active Top-Secret clearance issued by another U.S. government agency at the time of hire. AWS Certified Solutions Architect credential or an equivalent advanced cloud certification. Deep familiarity with hybrid cloud architectures and expert-level proficiency in integrating on-premises environments with cloud platforms in air-gapped environments. Comprehensive knowledge of compliance frameworks, such as National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), FedRAMP, and related standards, with proven experience implementing and maintaining compliance within cloud environments. This is a remote position with up to 50% domestic travel required. Candidates may reside in any state within the United States and should expect frequent national travel. The AbbVie Employer NAE is responsible for supporting and implementing strategic business initiatives in response to the changing healthcare environment, deployed specifically to national Employer Stakeholders via the AbbVie Employer Team with a focus on improving workforce health and productivity and maximizing strategic access to AbbVie’s therapies. The Employer NAE will be accountable for building effective stakeholder strategies and engagements that are on the forefront of emerging concerns impacting employee access, affordability, disease state awareness/management and medication value and access. This includes healthcare decision-makers (HCDMs) within national employer plan sponsors, employee benefit consultants (EBCs), and employer coalitions, as well as emerging stakeholders/influencers/vendors, national organizations, and professional/advocacy organizations. The Employer NAE provides branded and unbranded messaging to employers and employer influencers/KOLs regarding the value and differentiation of AbbVie therapies to accelerate access to treatment and the use of benefit plan designs to identify and minimize barriers to affordable and predictable Rx access. The NAE also delivers messaging relating to disease state and burden of illness to increase the awareness of treatment solutions and explore solutions and develop best practices/case studies. The Employer NAE will provide leadership to distinguish AbbVie in the employer channel, be a convener of stakeholders and regional/national KOLs and SMEs, and provide strategic insights internally in support of evolving business needs to ensure timely awareness of market changes and trends and inform internal business leads to ensure a rapid response to external disruptors and Rx management strategies which impact affordable access to AbbVie’s therapies. This role is highly collaborative and consultative and requires partnering and interfacing with numerous cross-functional teams (Market Access leadership, Payer Strategy and Cross Portfolio Strategy and Pipeline, Training, Market Analytics Business Insights, Business Evolution Strategy Development (BESD), Brand Sales/Marketing, Government Affairs and Policy, Corporate Strategy, US Medical Affairs/Value & Access and Medical Outcomes Science & Science Liaisons (MOSLs); Finance, Legal, Compliance, Communications/PR, Field Reimbursement Leadership, Brand Sales/Marketing teams and internal Centers of Excellence (CoE). The NAE must demonstrate the ability to anticipate and act proactively and effectively in uncertain situations. Additionally, the NAE requires significant collaboration with the Corporate Accounts KAM teams, providing timely insights regarding evolving contracting trends and evolving rebate models, educating client-facing teams, and providing updates regarding downstream employer clients and formulary initiatives. This position does not have direct reports but does require the ability to manage and lead without authority across cross-functional teams while also being able to work independently and productively. The Employer NAE is the lead for regional employer initiatives working in conjunction with the Regional Account Executive (RAE) teams and Regional Directors, as well as compliant collaboration with the Population Heath Account Executive (PHAE) team. This includes identifying opportunities and/or employer access issues and training/educating and executing on use of Employer Team resources and messaging to health plan, health system, PBM and employer customers. This role also is a key collaborator with other national field-based teams including the Field Reimbursement team, educating team members on market disruptors and problem-solving on employer-focused access issues. The Employer NAE serves as a key role in cataloguing key disruptors and potential patient disruption and analyzing potential financial (Gross to Net) impact, as well as working across internal stakeholders to develop and execute mitigation strategies. Major Duties and Responsibilities: Proactively engage with existing employer stakeholders and identify/influence emerging employer stakeholders across the US. Identify insights, positions and potential impact of new and emerging employer stakeholders and vendors. Build proactive share of voice with employer customers and influencers on Rx management topics. Support and contribute to internal Strategy Teams regarding emerging strategies and identification of external SMEs. Collaborate with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy Directors to connect and convene with new and emerging stakeholders and advocates. Work in conjunction with Employer Team Director and Marketing Director (and collaboratively with Principal National MOSL, Employer Channel) relative to employer channel resource development and messaging. Develop and deliver stakeholder appropriate resources to support access for the expanding AbbVie portfolio (DSA decks, case studies, condensed employer value-prop decks, case studies and benefit plan design resources) Cultivate national employer KOLs and advocates to help shape external education and policy in collaboration with Government Affairs/Policy/Strategy teams. Monitor, inform and deliver market insights to internal business partners. Lead education initiatives in conjunction with Market Access Training on key trends impacting purchasers and AbbVie access/gross-to-net. Establish AbbVie as credible source for non-branded information and disseminate via industry meetings and electronic sites / social media (consistent with AbbVie Communications/PR guidelines). Support efforts to integrate Employer Strategy into AbbVie Business Planning process. Assist AbbVie Employer Corporate Account Team Leader with managing budget and execution of sponsorships and memberships, consistent with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) guidelines. Establish AbbVie as a national leader and key partner in the employer channel. Work with Big 3 PBM/GPO KAM teams and respective rebate analysts to ensure contract compliance. Quantify volume/sales associated with employer child accounts and access changes. Participate in internal task forces relating to member/patient access. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Life Sciences, or a related field required. Minimum of 5 years of Account Executive or Market Access experience within the healthcare industry; employee benefits consulting (EBC) experience and/or PBM experience is a plus. Proven ability to operate effectively in large, complex geographies, influence diverse stakeholders, and deliver commercial results. Demonstrated capability in negotiation, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning/development and execution. Strong analytical skills, especially related to Rx contract terms/language and the commercial payor market. Effective communication and presentation skills (written and oral) with both technical and non-technical audiences. Experience managing complexity and collaborating with cross-functional, matrixed teams; agility and team-orientation required. Customer-centric approach and proven ability to act as primary point of contact for internal and external stakeholders. Ability to work autonomously, manage ambiguity, and identify/influence key customers. Understanding of the evolving healthcare environment—including ACA, CAA, ERISA, clinical guidelines, and formulary/utilization management. Adept at delivering product and disease state value proposition materials to a range of customers. Highest ethical standards and compliance with AbbVie Office of Ethics and Compliance (OEC) policies. Significant domestic travel required (up to 50%) for customer interactions, industry meetings and internal meetings. An essential requirement of your position is to satisfy all applicable health care industry representative (HCIR) credentialing requirements to gain and maintain entry into facilities and organizations that are in your assigned territory. You must also be in good standing and/or eligible to obtain these credentials. Driving a personal auto or company car or truck, or a powered piece of material handling equipment. Valid driver’s license: Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screening test and meet safe driving requirements. Preferred: 10+ years’ experience in pharmaceutical, Rx supply chain, employee benefit consulting, or healthcare organization. Deep understanding of commercial business models and payor markets.

Position Summary Machine/grind parts/tools to conform to blueprints/drawings Duties and responsibilities The following reflects management’s definition of essential functions for this job but does not restrict the tasks that may be assigned. Management may assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time due to reasonable accommodation or other reasons Maintain accurate inventory levels of CNC and HMC tooling, ensuring proper organization and storage. Inspect tooling for wear and determine when resharpening is required, coordinating with the manufacturer as needed. Perform grinding and relief operations on tooling as required. Assemble tooling for CNC and HMC machines as needed. Rework HMC manifold parts as required. Calibrate torque wrenches to ensure accuracy and compliance with standards. Machine and grind fixtures and parts as needed to support production. Operate CNC machines while adhering to blueprint specifications and quality standards. Conduct stability studies on gauges to ensure reliability and precision. Perform initial inspections of parts/tools when required. Support training efforts for manual machining processes. Maintain a clean and organized work while following 5S. Adhere to all safety, sanitation, and Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) requirements. Perform additional duties as assigned by the manager. Supervisory Responsibilities None Physical Requirements While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to do the following: Lift and move up to 50 pounds without assistance Able to stand for long periods of time Ability to load/unload machines (requires repetitive lifting and bending) Work Environment Majority of the work time is spent in a manufacturing environment where temperatures are often warm or cool, depending upon the season, and noise level can be moderate to high PPE required as determined by company safety standards: safety glasses, ear plugs, gloves, safety shoes Highschool diploma or equivalent preferred 5 or more years of experience as a toolmaker/machinist Demonstrated ability to setup and troubleshoot tooling issues Ability to assist/develop and or improve processes on new or existing parts with a complete understanding of machining fundamentals and practices Ability to use all relevant measurement equipment Ability to follow written and verbal instructions given in English Ability to meet quality and productivity standards Ability to read blueprints thoroughly Computer skills, intermediate knowledge Microsoft Office Strong attention to detail Ability to work as a part of a team Ability to be at workstation on time, every day unless authorized

Specializes in working in facilities that manufacture a finished product for sale, or sale to another organization for use in an end product. Performs microbial control cleaning procedures that must comply with current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and regulatory guidelines which include documentation of work procedures frequently audited by the FDA and other regulatory agencies. The work will be accomplished under the general supervision of Lead Personnel and an area Supervisor. Responsibilities Performs cross contamination cleaning methods in areas that require microbial control. Completes cGMP documentation of training or cleaning performed on paper and electronic devices. Prepares cleaning solutions based on cGMP regulated mixing instructions. Performs microbial control cleaning techniques on walls, ceiling and floors based on cGMP regulated cleaning frequencies. Completes preventive maintenance work orders to meet cGMP cleaning requirements. Follows specific gowning procedures and performs cGMP entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments. Operates bailing and compacting equipment. Operates various types of hand held battery and electric cleaning equipment. Operates various types of battery and electric walk behind or ride-on floor cleaning equipment. Performs safety and preventive maintenance inspections on housekeeping power equipment and small tools and wears approved PPE. High School Diploma or equivalent. Must be able to read and comprehend written information to include Corporate Quality Documents, Divisional Operating Procedures, Departmental Operating Procedures and Safety Guidelines. Must be able to comply with cGMP, regulatory guidelines and able to write legibility in English and complete accurate and legible written records in compliance with cGMP when documenting work performed, on paper documents and electronic devices auditable by regulatory agencies. Must be able to operate a computer to complete required compliance & technical training. Must have the ability to learn and perform cleaning techniques to meet regulatory requirements. Must have the ability to work alone or as a team member sharing responsibility and work tasks. Must be able to perform all cleaning specialist job functions. Basic physical requirements are but are not limited to: stand for 7 hours per shift, regularly lift 35 pounds 50 times per shift, occasionally lift 50 pounds 6 times per shift, walk approximately 2000 feet per hour, climb 6 flights of stairs per shift, work on knees 30 minutes per shift, bend / Squat 200 times per shift, rotate left / right 200 times per shift.

Workflow Management & Process Optimization Manage the full graphics production pipeline from concept to on-air execution Organize and maintain a centralized graphics asset library with proper version control and archiving Establish, document, and improve efficient workflows and best practices Track and report on project deliverables and performance metrics Assist with hardware/software upgrades and studio builds 3. Collaboration & Live Production Support Collaborate with producers, directors, show teams, and technical staff to meet project goals Serve as a primary contact for troubleshooting real-time graphics issues during live broadcasts Support graphics playout in live event and studio environments Work closely with production teams to design graphics tailored to specific programs or segments Communicate clearly with to manage expectations and ensure timely delivery Independently research and resolve technical challenges 4. Position Purpose: Installs and repairs all electrical work throughout the treatment distribution system. Performs electrical work to maintain, install, repair or alter electrical systems found in treatment and pumping facilities, including electrical construction, installation, maintenance, and repair. Primary Duties/Responsibilities: Troubleshoot malfunctioning equipment to determine the nature of the problem, repair small and large electrical appliances, repair electronic components of electrical equipment as required for continued operations, make emergency electrical repairs to generators and pumps, and perform related duties as required; and perform related duties as assigned. Perform electrical work to maintain, install or repair all electrical systems, facilities and pump stations. Repair or replace defective or worn electrical parts, components and controlling software in electrical systems and devices, electrical motors, generators, pumps, controllers, lighting systems, and other fixtures and equipment. Work independently and make sound decisions regarding work methods and tools; read, interpret, apply, and enforce applicable codes and standards as related to electrical installation; apply State, Federal, and local safety regulations and codes to electrical work. Work safely both independently and as a crew member on high voltages up to 600 volts AC; work safely near energized primary and secondary lines with voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Read and works from electrical blueprints and drawings. Comprehend and make inferences from written material; read and interpret blueprints, wiring diagrams, and work orders. Perform preventative maintenance on electrical systems, motors and equipment. Inspect newly installed electrical equipment and lighting to ensure safe operation as well as code compliance. Maintain accurate records of work performed, materials used, and associated costs. Perform associated work including digging, trenching, occasional concrete finishing and removal, and lifting electrical equipment, conduit and pipe. Replaces defective wiring. Control wiring experience required. Variable Frequency Drive experience recommended. Work Environment: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is routinely exposed to a variety of outside weather conditions, including very hot temperatures. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. This employee can work in high voltages up to 600 Volts AC. Education/Experience/Background: High School Diploma/GED is required. 5 years journey level electrical experience required. Knowledge/Skills/Abilities: Knowledge of methods, materials, tools, equipment, and procedures used in the installation, maintenance, repair, replacement and alteration of electrical equipment; components and parts used in modern electrical wiring systems such as pumps, motors, controls and lighting. Basic understanding of overhead line construction, Nation Electric Code and Federal and State OSHA standards. Read, interpret and enforce applicable State and Federal codes and requirements. Ability to communicate with all levels including team, management, clients, and vendors in a professional manner both orally and in writing. Safety procedures in electrical maintenance and operations. The employee must be able to operate electric motors fueled by gasoline, diesel, or gaseous fuels, paint, welding, and fabrication equipment, and other hand tools required. Required Certification/Licenses/Training: Valid industrial electrician’s license preferred. Physical Requirements: The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, climb stairs or ladders, sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl and taste or smell. The employee may regularly lift 10-20 pounds and may occasionally lift and or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include the ability to distinguish color, close vision and distance vision.

Build and maintain analytical models in Excel, Python, or SQL to support scenario planning, freight benchmarking, and lane-level performance analysis. Synthesize large, multi-source datasets into concise, meaningful narratives that highlight the "so what" behind the numbers for non-technical stakeholders. Prepare executive-ready data packages, briefing decks, and slide materials for business reviews, QBRs, Board presentations, and leadership offsites. Work with IT and data engineering teams to establish reliable data pipelines feeding Power BI from source systems including EDW, TMS, carrier portals, and third-party visibility platforms. Continuously improve report usability and performance based on stakeholder feedback, usage analytics, and emerging Power BI capabilities. Required Experience & Education Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Data Analytics, Industrial Engineering, Information Systems, Business, or a related quantitative field. 0–5 years+ of experience in supply chain analysis, logistics analytics, or a closely related data-intensive role within a global enterprise. Advanced proficiency in Power BI, including data modeling, DAX, Power Query (M language), report design, and workspace administration. Strong SQL skills for querying relational databases and building data extracts from ERP and operational systems. Python or R (preferred): Strong command of data visualization principles—ability to select the right chart type, structure narratives, and tailor outputs for executive audiences. Data Visualization: Familiarity with Oracle Cloud, OTM, GTM platforms, or freight visibility tools. THE POSITION: Medical Information is a critically important customer-facing function that supports the safe and effective use of pharmaceutical company products by providing timely, scientifically balanced, evidence based, nonpromotional information in response to unsolicited requests from healthcare professionals, patients, caregivers, and payers. Medical Information also plays an important role in post-marketing handling of adverse events and product complaints. As part of the Medical Information Contact Center (MICC) team, this position delivers industry-leading services, which include Contact Center staffing for responding to product information requests, identifying and handling of adverse events and/or product quality issues, and medical writing as needed to generate written response for use in response to medical questions received. This position requires clinical and therapeutic knowledge, critical and analytical thinking, and customer/patient-centric approach. Medical Information Specialists typically support multiple pharmaceutical clients, multiple products, and multiple therapeutic areas. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES: Our employees are tasked with delivering excellent business results through the efforts of their teams. These results are achieved by: MEDICAL INFORMATION SUPPORT Respond to medical information inquiries from physicians, pharmacists, nurses, and other health care professionals, consumers, and payers. Utilize medical information skills to identify, research, and critically evaluate medical literature to create responses to medical information inquiries. Utilize writing skills for adverse event and product complaint narrative during intake as well as medical inquiry custom responses. Handle requests across multiple channels and platforms (phone, email, CRM, chat, etc.) Identify adverse events and product complaints during interactions with customers. Perform intake sufficient to generate adverse event and product complaint reports in compliance with EVERSANA-MICC and client standard operating procedures. Knowledge of FDA’s postmarketing adverse event reporting regulations and safety terminology. Ability to make accurate assessments regarding what information needs to be obtained and level or depth of information to be collected. Coordinate processes necessary for responding to product quality-related complaints. This process may involve interactions with personnel in the following departments: Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and the complainant. Maintain product, therapeutic area, and client specific requirements knowledge. Ensure good documentation, high quality, and excellent customer service. Medical writing and Medical Information content development. Provide medical writing to assist in drafting of Medical Information response documents [FAQs, Scientific Response Documents (SRDs), Custom Response Documents (CRDs)] and/or work collaboratively with medical writing team to develop these materials.  Staffing at scientific medical affairs booths. On-call responsibilities on an as assigned basis. Miscellaneous projects such as market and competitive product research, operational and process improvements, field team training and field liaison support.  All other duties as assigned. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position. Customer Services: Maintain and improve customer services associated with activity of the Medical Communications Contact Center. Hours: Able to work full time and be flexible with work scheduling as required by clients and management. WTVJ is seeking a strong journalist with a passion for news to put an emphasis on content when producing for multiple platforms. You’ll need to line produce, write, copyedit, edit video, gather content and produce elements all under heavy deadline pressure, without compromising accuracy and credibility. TRAINING The Sales Trainee (ST) is a training role. Upon successful participation in the training program, the ST is eligible to interview for open Account Sales Manager (ASM) roles. Upon completion of the program and certification, if no ASM or otherwise qualified role is available AND the ST is meeting performance standards, the employee may remain in the ST role up to 12-months OR until an ASM or another qualified role is available (whichever comes first). Once an ASM or another qualified role is available, the certified ST must interview for that available role. If promotion to the role of ACCOUNT SALES MANAGER (or other role) does not happen prior to the expiration of the 12-mos completion period, the SALES TRAINEE role will be vacated due to end of assignment unless an exception applies. For exception, based on continued high performance, no open roles and certification completion, a manager may extend the 12-month completion period an additional 6-months. The ST role is an at-will position, meaning that the Company or ST can terminate the employment relationship at any time, for any reason or no reason at all, with or without cause. Job Description: NBC Sports is looking for a social marketing strategist to join our team – a detail-minded and collaborative team member who’s passionate about how to blend data and insights into actionable content strategy for NBC Sports and its portfolio of brands. In this role, you’ll work with the Director, Social Strategy & Insights to support strategy development and content analysis, a critical part of the team that connects audience insights and creative ideas to brand priorities and making sure everyone has the information they need to deliver their best work. The Person: You’re energized by the idea of connecting strategy to storytelling that audiences love. You’re organized, proactive, and ready to jump in wherever you can to help – whether that’s pulling insights, building presentations, or keeping timelines straight. You adapt quickly, collaborate easily with different personalities and disciplines, and aren’t shy about asking thoughtful questions. You keep things moving forward with a positive, solutions-oriented mindset. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to: Support the development of strategic briefs and presentations, gathering inputs from multiple stakeholders. Manage business critical social insights workflows, including content tagging, data analysis and content evaluation Coordinate with Sports Marketing group to align with key business priorities, including short and long-term social strategy development Compile and summarize competitive and industry research to help inform social marketing strategies Organize and maintain engagement and growth vitals on the full suite of NBC Sports properties, making it easy for team to quickly access relevant insights and updates. Basic Requirements: 1+ years of relevant experience in marketing, media, communications, data and analytics, or related field Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to organize information clearly Proficiency in Microsoft Office and various social data and management platforms (Hootsuite, Sprout Social, Sprinklr or similar) Comfortability managing multiple tasks simultaneously, in which no task is too big or small Curiosity and willingness to learn new tools and processes Demonstrated interest in sports and entertainment programming and brand marketing Strong work ethic, with a dedication to excellence and exceptional attention to detail Desired Characteristics: Bachelor’s Degree preferred Experience in basic data analysis is required Additional Requirements: Hybrid : This position currently has a hybrid schedule, which requires contributing from the office a minimum of four days per week. This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks. Learn more about the benefits offered by NBCUniversal by visiting the Benefits page of the Careers website. Salary range: $50,000- $60,000

We have an opening for a Field Technician to provide technical support and customer services in the management of hazardous and radioactive waste. Under general supervision you will perform a variety of technical functions in collecting, packaging, labeling, identifying, documenting, segregating, consolidating, treating, and storing hazardous, explosive and radioactive waste generated by various LLNL programs. This position is in the Radioactive and Hazardous Waste Management (RHWM) Program and part of the Special Project Group supporting Site 200 within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position requires full-time on-site presence due to the nature of the work. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Perform a wide variety of waste management activities, often wearing personal protective equipment (PPE) such as anti-C’s, respirator, hearing protection, etc., to collect, package, label, identify, segregate, consolidate, treat, store, and verify hazardous, low level radioactive, mixed and/or transuranic waste. Operate wastewater retention tanks and/or systems, perform pump-outs, perform lab packing of waste chemicals and manage waste container storage areas. Perform field testing (pH, visual etc.) and sampling of waste to verify characterization and/or treatment results and operate radiation survey instruments to obtain radiological data. Operate a variety of vehicles up to and including 5-ton trucks, use material handling equipment (fork trucks, drum handling equipment, mechanical pump systems, etc.), and use hand and power tools. Respond to environmental emergencies at LLNL and work with cross-organizational personnel performing decontamination of facility infrastructure and equipment. Gather, analyze, and record basic pertinent data and maintain detailed and accurate records associated with radioactive and hazardous waste to properly characterize and manage the waste. Complete and maintain training requirements per Federal, State, and LLNL requirements. Provide high-end customer service with a wide range of waste generators as the front-line interface between RHWM and waste generators. Support various scope Decontamination and Demolition (D&D) projects on behalf of LLNL. Perform all assignments in accordance with ES&H, security, and business practice requirements and policies. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities at the 504.3 Level Solve difficult radioactive and hazardous waste management problems using established guidelines and routine techniques and procedures. Plan and execute waste management projects including directing the activities of other technicians. Conduct On-the-Job-Training and provide mentoring and leadership for less experienced technicians. Act as Responsible Individual (RI) on Work Control Documents. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q-level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate degree in environmental or related scientific field, or equivalent combination of education and experience. Intermediate knowledge of State and Federal regulations as they apply to hazardous and radioactive waste management, with emphasis on managing waste in satellite accumulation areas (SAAs) and 90-day consolidated accumulation areas (CAAs) or experience working within nuclear or high-hazard facilities. Intermediate knowledge of field instrumentation, such as radiation survey instruments, pH meters, etc., with an emphasis on their application to radioactive and hazardous waste processes. Elementary understanding of chemistry principles, including compatibility, and/or general understanding of radioactive contamination control methods. Ability to meet medical qualification to wear respiratory protection equipment, climb ladders and meet other physical requirements specified in the job demands worksheet and to successfully complete all Federal, State, LLNL and Department of Transportation (DOT) training requirements. Effective communication and interpersonal skills in order to build and maintain working relationships with coworkers, waste generators, programmatic support personnel and management. Strong organizational skills with the ability to generate and maintain high-quality, accurate records and correspondence using PC and/or Apple workstations and associated applications. Effective customer service skills needed to provide waste management support to a wide range of waste generators. Additional qualifications at the 504.3 Level Experience managing projects with minimal direction needed. High level understanding and knowledge of State and Federal regulations (RCRA, DOE, DOT) applicable to waste management, with demonstrated experience in their application or extensive experience working within nuclear facilities with a proven track record of accomplishing tasks while following strict controls. Experience with contaminated facility D&D. Experience providing training and mentoring to less experienced personnel. Pay Range $43.55 - $63.97 Hourly $43.55 - $53.36 Hourly for the 504.2 level $52.23 - $63.97 Hourly for the 504.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

We have an opening for a Document Compliance Coordinator to navigate a complex matrix of federal, institutional and organizational requirements. You will collaborate with engineers and subject matter experts to initiate, develop, document and evaluate comprehensive technical procedures, documents and safety plans. This position will support the Superblock (SBK) facility within the Strategic Deterrence Directorate. This position may offer a hybrid schedule, which includes the flexibility to work from home one or more days per week, after a probationary period. The specifics of the hybrid schedule, including the exact number of days required in the office and virtual work options, may vary based on the needs of the team and the organization. This position will be filled at either level based on knowledge and related experience as assessed by the hiring team. Additional job responsibilities (outlined below) will be assigned if hired at the higher level. In this role you will Analyze and implement documentation processes, procedures, and practices to ensure activities within the facility are performed in compliance with requirements in federal regulations, institutional procedures, and the nuclear facility safety bases. Evaluate procedures and process documents to verify facility requirements are adequately implemented, controls identified in the safety basis documents are maintained, and technical and management reviews are conducted. Serve as a contact for SBK processes, procedures, practices, manuals, guidance documents and safety plans and provide guidance to others related to SBK administrative procedures associated with document compliance. Collaborate with subject matter experts to initiate, develop, review, revise, implement and evaluate documentation that impact SBK facilities and systems, as well as LLNL programs. Monitor document tracking and routing, and ensure revision control using electronic applications (e.g., Enterprise Lifecycle Management-Unclassified [ELM-U]/Windchill) for configuration management of documents. Assist in planning, coordinating, and conducting periodic assessments to determine conformance with regulations, LLNL requirements, and SBK plans and procedures, including management self-assessments, observations and inspections, relating to SBK processes and other operational activities; recommend and coordinate completion of corrective action plans related to deficiencies. Manage technical information communications and interface with the LLNL programs and facilities personnel related to facility procedures; solicit feedback and facilitate comment resolution. Perform other duties as assigned. Additional job responsibilities, at the A23.3 level Develop, plan, review, assess, analyze, and implement administrative processes, procedures, and practices by applying in depth knowledge to ensure SBK activities comply with governing requirements, including federal regulations, LLNL procedures, and nuclear facility safety basis documents. Provide professional support to program/practice/policy development and implementation efforts; assists with program research and ongoing monitoring of results. Serves as a subject matter expert and trusted resource, providing informed recommendations to management on policy updates and changes. Ability to secure and maintain a U.S. DOE Q level security clearance which requires U.S. citizenship. Associate Degree in a related field or equivalent combination of education and related experience in a business, operational and/or organizational area. Experience interpreting, reviewing and analyzing administrative processes, policies, procedures and practices to determine if the activities they address are performed in compliance with complex regulations and requirements. Effective technical composition, writing and editing skills and experience effectively composing professional documentation with the ability to obtain a Procedure Professionals Association (PPA) Certification. Experience tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to coordinate corrective actions. Proficient verbal and written communication skills necessary to manage scientific and technical communications across multidisciplinary teams, with effective collaboration and communication skills necessary to effectively explain and present proposed changes to documents and processes. Effective organizational and interpersonal skills necessary to resolve problems and sensitive/confidential issues with tact, discretion, and mature judgment. Strong proficiency in Microsoft Word and a solid working knowledge of Excel, FileMaker Pro, Adobe Acrobat, and EDMS (such as SharePoint or Windchill) with the ability to learn new software quickly. Additional qualifications at the A23.3 level Experience researching, tracking, compiling and monitoring data necessary to conduct self-assessment activities, effectively present findings, and coordinate corrective actions. Broad and specialized knowledge of and experience in related work activities and multi-faceted internal processes. Experience training and mentoring personnel on document control within a regulated environment, ensuring compliance with applicable requirements. Pay Range $94,560 - $138,888 Annually $94,560 - $115,728 Annually for the A23.2 level $113,400 - $138,888 Annually for the A23.3 level This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

Position Purpose: This position is for the Energy Markets and Sustainability Services group at Veolia North America. Broadly, our team helps customers navigate the complexity of energy and sustainability markets with a focus on consulting & brokering for wholesale electricity and natural gas transactions. Ultimately, our role is to provide clients with market insight needed to make strategic decisions when purchasing energy, navigating sustainability initiatives, managing budgetary risk and reducing energy spend. This position will include meeting with clients to discuss their energy needs, researching and modeling energy policies and tariffs, creating energy budgets for clients, and much more. Co-ops are full-time team members who are treated and valued as such! They are fully integrated into the Energy Markets and Sustainability Services team - working alongside everybody and being pulled into a host of projects, client meetings, etc. On our team, we make an intentional effort to integrate our co-ops throughout our work to provide them with the most valuable experience possible based on their personal goals. Develop Excel-based energy market analytical models, incorporating historical natural gas and electricity data, futures contracts, and cost inputs at different S. locations to be utilized internally and presented to clients. Develop client energy budgets, evaluate client electricity / natural gas contract performance, model client distribution tariffs, and audit client energy invoices. Perform energy procurement activities such as creating requests for proposals (RFPs), assist in formulating hedging strategies, communicating with customers and suppliers, and contributing to advisory calls. Create presentation materials for market updates. Relevant materials include natural gas supply, demand, and storage conditions, national weather forecasts, and regulatory development. Perform market research as necessary to help manage client needs. Good communication, interpersonal skills, and teamwork. Curiosity and a willingness to learn. Proficiency with Excel. A self-starter attitude.

Company Overview At Motorola Solutions, we believe that everything starts with our people. We’re a global close-knit community, united by the relentless pursuit to help keep people safer everywhere. We build and connect technologies to help protect people, property and places. Our solutions foster the collaboration that’s critical for safer communities, safer schools, safer hospitals, safer businesses, and ultimately, safer nations. Connect with a career that matters, and help us build a safer future. Department Overview It’s not just about having the right technology; it’s about achieving peak performance. Motorola Solutions has served as a trusted partner to government agencies and enterprises worldwide for more than 95 years. Our years of leadership, innovation and experience managing and supporting hundreds of networks in more than 100 countries help answer the challenges of mission critical operations – ensure continuity, enhance productivity and reduce risk – helping achieve peak performance. When every second counts and performance reliability is a must – we are ready and able to serve today, tomorrow and into the future. Motorola Solutions is a world leader in the field of professional mobile communications systems with an impressive heritage of technological innovations and a global base of installed systems. The FSO (Field Service Organization) is responsible for supporting the implementation and maintenance of highly technical mission critical communications systems at customer locations. Job Description The job tasks encompass a wide range of technical responsibilities, including the deployment, optimization, and repair of infrastructure, public safety loggers, subscribers, microwave equipment, computers, servers, and network equipment. The FSO collaborates closely with Public Safety Customers, System Managers, Engineers, Sales Teams, Project Managers, System Technologists, and Service Partners to successfully complete assigned tasks. Additionally, the department operates on a 24/7/365 basis to provide support for mission-critical systems that serve our Public Safety Customers. Maintain, optimize, test, document and manage highly technical Motorola communications systems. Focus on maintaining optimal performance levels across an integrated system while taking a proactive approach to address and mitigate system level alarms and malfunctions. Manage system availability through routine system maintenance, performance monitoring and system wide preventative maintenance. Perform preventative maintenance routines to ensure proper system operation with focus on trend analysis and the documentation of results. Optimize and support complex communication systems and software applications, including advanced troubleshooting of software driven electronics, provisioning of communication system infrastructure and performance optimization of RF and Broadband systems. Deliver knowledge of R.F. systems, such as transmitters, receivers, and antenna networks. Deliver knowledge in standard telephony, dedicated data circuits, and packet switching techniques. Provide weekly reports of activities and accomplishments. Develop solutions to difficult technical problems encountered as part of system maintenance, upgrades or support issues. Continuous training in the latest technologies and troubleshooting techniques. Team with Engineering, Project Management, Customer Service and Sales personnel to effectively maintain, optimize and support advanced communication systems which meet or exceed customer expectations. Preferred Skills: Candidates must be familiar with the latest technologies and troubleshooting techniques for current model digital and analog Motorola communications equipment and system architectures. Experience as a Communications System Technician with expertise in P25 Systems, LMR RF systems, wired/wireless communication systems, networking equipment, IT networks, and subscriber equipment. Highly knowledgeable in wired/wireless communications systems, including local area networks (LAN) and wide area networks (WAN). The ideal candidate should possess a strong understanding and awareness of cybersecurity principles and practices. Proficient in Google Suite, MS Word, Excel, Outlook, and Access, demonstrating strong computer literacy. Possesses exceptional self-management and interpersonal skills to effectively collaborate with customers, subcontractor partners, and various teams within Motorola Solutions. Self-motivated and capable of performing duties independently without direct supervision. Skilled in quickly resolving customer problems even in stressful situations. Familiarity with configuring and testing base stations, repeaters, routers, switches, and MPLS networks. Proficient in installing, configuring, and maintaining computer networks, including cabling, routers, switches, firewalls, and bridges. Ability to develop and deliver technical training. Provides guidance on integrating new tools and solutions into team operations. Proven experience utilizing equipment commonly used for optimizing and testing Motorola communications systems, such as Communications Systems Analyzers, Power Sensors and Watt Meters, TIMS sets, CPS, CSS, Antenna Systems Analyzers (FDRs). Skilled in configuring and testing Motorola two-way radio and subscriber products. Experience working with logging recording systems, RF interfaces, wired/wireless communications systems, 911 applications, and networking equipment. Candidate Requirements: The Field Service Technician MUST live a commutable distance to the Miami Dade County area. Must be willing to travel 25% of the time and live within 50 miles from the coverage area. Must be able to obtain background clearance as required by government customer(s). Must have a current, valid driver’s license and no traffic violations. Ability to be on-call 24/7/365 FCC license and industry certifications such as ETA are a plus. CET certifications through CompTIA Network+ and/or Security+ are highly desirable. Legal authorization to work in the U.S. indefinitely is required. Employer work permit sponsorship is not available for this position. Seeking a Records Management Analyst to support the Records Management Group (RMG) for a US government customer. This person will ensure the RMG follows the Federal Records Management Act and all related statutes, federal regulations, and customer and Intelligence Community (IC) policies and procedures. This includes but is not limited to requirements set forth in the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), United States Code (USC), and National Archives and Records Administration (NARA) mandates. Deliver customer support and training on records management to customer personnel. Consult and coordinate with Intelligence Community (IC) elements on the development and consistent implementation of IC records management policies and procedures, utilize proper handling of classified records and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) records, and support the Information Management Council (IMC) and other IC records management committees. Advise government offices in their efforts to reorder and clean their Shared Drive and support the implementation of a customer electronic records management system (ERMS). Develop and implement plans for customer essential records identification and protection. Provide inputs to annual compliance reports as directed by the government staff. Support records management system reviews and implementation. Active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph is required. The Role We are seeking a Computational Mechanics and Computer Aided Design Researcher to join our Design for X ( DfX ) team within Research & Development. In this role, you will help shape the future of engineering design by developing AI powered tools embedded directly into our CAD workflow ( Siemens NX ) , enabling engineers to create designs that are optimized for performance, manufacturability, and quality before production begins. This position sits at the intersection of computational geometry, mechanics, and artificial intelligence, translating advanced research into practical, CAD native engineering capabilities used at scale. You will play a key role in advancing our capabilities and ensuring that our products are at the forefront of the industry . What You'll Do Develop computational geometry and mechanics algorithms that reason directly on CAD models to support design evaluation and optimization. Research and prototype AI assisted generative design workflows that combine data driven methods with physics and geometry aware reasoning. Build CAD integrated solutions within Siemens NX to enable pushbutton analysis, design exploration, and manufacturability checks. Design and validate methods that balance learning based approaches with deterministic evaluation, ensuring results are explainable and repeatable. Collaborate with cross functional partners in R&D, Manufacturing, Product Engineering and IT to transition research concepts into scalable engineering tools. Communicate research outcomes through technical reports, demonstrations, and presentations to engineering and leadership audiences. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): PhD in Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Computer Graphics, or a related field . OR MS Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Computer Graphics, or a related field and 2 + years of equivalent experience. Strong background in computational mechanics, numerical methods, or simulation - driven design. Expertise in computational geometry or computer graphics, such as surface representations, geometry processing, feature detection, or geometric optimization. Proficiency in Python and/ or C / C # /C++ for algorithm development and research prototyping. Experience applying machine learning to engineering or geometry - centric problems. Ability to design rigorous experiments and validate results using appropriate engineering metrics. Strong written and verbal communication skills What Will Give You A Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): Experience developing CAD or CAE integrations, particularly with Siemens NX or similar platforms. Familiarity with DFX, manufacturability analysis, or CAD based checking tools. Experience combining physics - based simulation with AI, such as surrogate modeling or physics informed ML. Background in manufacturing related mechanics (e.g., forming, joining, structural performance). Publication or patent record in computational mechanics, geometry processing, or AI for engineering. AbbVie’s Analytics and Performance Excellence (APEX) function is seeking a highly strategic, analytical, and collaborative Associate Director to provide analytics leadership for the Business Evolution Strategic Development (BESD) Team. This role will drive impactful business analytics and insights to help AbbVie anticipate and navigate evolving healthcare environments, especially focusing on market access and policy disruptors. The Associate Director will bridge Market Access and Patient Services (MAPS) Team within APEX and BESD (Business Evolution Strategic Development) team objectives by leading modelling, advanced insights and analytics supporting forward-looking strategies, enabling enterprise readiness, and shaping market access policies and outcomes for AbbVie’s diverse U.S. portfolio. This role requires a strong grasp of healthcare policy, payer analytics, and strategy formulation within a collaborative, cross-functional environment. Key Responsibilities: Lead the planning and execution of analytics to inform market access strategies, price reform and policy analysis, with actionable recommendations for AbbVie leadership. Identify payer opportunities/threats through deep dive analytics ('Follow the Dollar', claims analysis, and scenario modeling). Foster positive relationships and close collaboration with teams including Government Affairs, Finance, Legal, Corporate Affairs, Brand, and Market Access. Communicate complex findings and insight-driven narratives to senior leadership and cross-functional teams, enabling improved payer knowledge and strategic decision-making. Monitor external environment and translate emerging trends (political, regulatory, legislative, commercial) into strategic recommendations for AbbVie’s business evolution. Advise on analytics infrastructure enhancements to drive business impact. Skills Action and Accountability: Own responsibility for activities within relevant workstreams, and engage and inspire cross functional stakeholders to advance towards clear objectives and strategies; make quick, but informed decisions, as appropriate, to ensure best paths forward in the midst of change market and policy dynamics. Constantly engage, guide, and support cross-functional team to address roadblocks, challenges, resourcing constraints and other dynamics. Leadership and Influence: Influence and persuade across multiple external and internal stakeholders. Collaboration and Teamwork: Work effectively with internal stakeholders, external market experts and partners. Bachelor’s degree required; master’s degree (MBA or related business/science) preferred. 10+ years of progressive analytical/ insights experience in healthcare industry (pharma, consulting, government affairs, market access, public policy, etc.). 1-2 years pharmaceutical market access experience with deep understanding of Health Plans, PBMs, Hospitals, Specialty Pharmacies, and healthcare policy stakeholders. Strong insurance channel experience and understanding (i.e. Medicare, Commercial etc.) Strong business acumen, strategic and analytical thinking, and executive presence. Exceptional communication and influencing skills, with the ability to distill complex information into compelling, concise messages. Strong organizational skills, flexibility, attention to detail, and experience in collaborative, dynamic environments. Exceptional communications and executive presence, critical thinking and interpersonal skills, strong ability to influence without authority, the ability to speak and write persuasively and with clarity, strong organizational skills, flexibility, and adaptability to changing requirements, resourcefulness and creativity, strong attention to detail, a proven track record of being able to work drive towards deadlines and an ability to work collaboratively in a fluid organizational and external environment. Must be an individual who works well in a team environment and enjoys working in a collegial, collaborative and fun, yet highly demanding culture Preferred: Experience in policy shaping, price reform strategy, and enterprise-level stakeholder partnership. Proficiency with pharmaceutical data sources (formulary, claims).

AI.Accelerate Overview: Are you a technically curious and ambitious undergraduate student with a passion for Artificial Intelligence? ServiceNow invites you to explore our AI.Accelerate program where you can develop practical AI skills and gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced, and immersive environment. This eight-week unpaid bootcamp is designed to provide a comprehensive introduction to the core concepts and techniques of AI, with a focus on practical application and real-world problem-solving. You'll learn from experienced instructors, work on challenging projects, and collaborate with a cohort of talented peers. Dates: June 15 – July 31, 2026 (Virtual) + Week 8—beginning of August (In Person) Location: Virtually via Zoom Duration: 4 hours a week (plus homework) What You'll Learn: Agentic AI Foundations: Understand what makes an AI system "agentic" — including autonomy, reasoning, and action-taking — and how LLMs are evolving from chat tools into decision-making agents. Agentic Design Patterns: Explore key architectural patterns including React, chain-of-thought, tool use, and memory, and understand the difference between single-agent and multi-agent systems and when to use each. Prompt Engineering: Learn techniques for writing reliable, production-grade prompts that drive consistent and predictable agent behavior at scale. Building Agents: Design agents that use tools, APIs, and external data sources, and learn how to structure agent memory — both short-term and long-term — for complex, multi-step tasks. Multi-Agent Orchestration: Build and manage multi-agent workflows where agents collaborate, delegate, and hand off tasks to accomplish goals that no single agent could complete alone. Evaluation Frameworks: Learn why evaluations are the most critical part of building AI systems and how to design frameworks that define what to measure and how to measure it effectively. AI Safety & Responsible Use: Understand real-world failure modes including hallucination, prompt injection, and behavioral drift, and learn how to build guardrails and safety checks into agentic pipelines. Capstone Project: Design, build, evaluate, and defend an AI agent from scratch — putting every concept from the program into practice and presenting your work to a panel of ServiceNow engineers and leaders. Innovative Learning Structure: A blend of lectures, hands-on laboratories, and collaborative projects fostering a cohort- based, hands on learning experience. The program concludes with an in-person experience where participants showcase their capstone project, explore career opportunities at ServiceNow, and connect with the broader engineering community. please note: this is an unpaid program and is not an internship To be successful in this role you: Have experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry . Are an Undergraduate student majoring or minoring in Computer Science (CS), Computer Engineering (CE), or Data Analytics. or related field, with a graduation date no earlier than December 2027 Are experienced in Python programming. Are experienced with and/or have knowledge of fundamental AI concepts Have availability to attend the full duration of the boot camp from June 15, 2026 to July 31, 2026 and then available to participate onsite in the beginning of August Application Process: Interested candidates should apply by April 15, 2026 , to be considered. Applications are evaluated until the application deadline only; therefore, early submission is recommended as spots are limited! Please submit a resume, a cover letter, and any related project work or AI experience. In your cover letter please share: Why do you want to participate in this AI bootcamp? Where do you see AI helping you in the future?

The AbbVie Process Chemistry Chromatographic Separations Lab is actively seeking an Associate Scientist II or Scientist I. Our team collaborates with colleagues across multiple disciplines, offering expertise in preparative chromatography to support a broad range of AbbVie R&D programs. We maintain and utilize specialized equipment for various separation tasks, including the purification of peptides, ADC drug-linkers, and chiral compounds, as well as the isolation of low-level API impurities. Additionally, the team is responsible for pilot-scale preparative purification, developing scalable purification processes, and overseeing their implementation under cGMP guidelines at AbbVie's North Chicago Chemical Pilot Plant. This role will contribute to the development of novel/advanced separations technologies and broader efforts to develop new process technologies for advancing the AbbVie pipeline. We are seeking a motivated scientist who demonstrates initiative and technical proficiency in supporting research and development projects within a collaborative team environment. The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience developing chromatographic methods and troubleshooting complex separation challenges. Experience working with peptides is highly desirable, but not required for application. Key Responsibilities: Develop and execute purification processes supporting development of small molecule, antibody drug conjugate, and peptide clinical candidates. Demonstrate scientific initiative and creativity in planning, executing, and troubleshooting experiments, resolving key project challenges with an appropriate level of autonomy based on experience. Conduct a range of laboratory and pilot-scale tasks, analyze and interpret data, and drive project objectives, assuming responsibility for tasks in accordance with experience. Suggest, adapt, and, as appropriate, implement new or improved experimental protocols/techniques, consulting relevant literature as needed. Build and maintain strong collaborative relationships with peers and cross-functional partners. Foster a learning environment, encourage diverse ideas, and support continuous process improvement. Understand and adhere strictly to corporate standards for conduct, safety, quality, and proper handling of materials. Bachelor’s degree with at least 3 years (Associate Scientist II) or 5 years (Scientist I) relevant experience; or Master’s degree with no additional experience (Associate Scientist II) or typically +2 years of relevant experience (Scientist I). Strong technical background in Separations Science, with theoretical and practical knowledge required to independently carry out job functions. Demonstrated proficiency in developing, troubleshooting, and modifying chromatographic methods and purification protocols. Broad expertise in analytical techniques, with emphasis on chromatography, compound purification, and spectral analysis. Ability to search scientific literature and evaluate potential solutions to research problems. Effective written and oral communication skills; able to work collaboratively in multidisciplinary teams.

At Visa, AI is central to our vision for the future of payments and commerce. The AI Center of Excellence (AI COE), part of the Global Data Office, is at the forefront of this mission—developing reusable AI/ML frameworks, enabling agentic AI workflows, and accelerating innovation across Visa’s data science community. The AI COE operates as both an enterprise capability builder and an AI SWAT team, tackling high-impact projects that address complex business challenges and create scalable, reusable solutions. From evaluating cutting-edge AI methods to deploying reusable frameworks in production, our mission is to improve efficiency, adoption, and business outcomes across Visa’s global Data & AI ecosystem. We are seeking an AI COE Analyst to contribute to technically complex AI initiatives—from research and prototyping through deployment—while advancing reusable AI capabilities and accelerating adoption across Visa. The AI COE Analyst will: Design, develop, and deploy advanced AI/ML methods and agentic AI workflows that address high-value challenges across Visa. Contribute to the creation of reusable AI frameworks, components, and internal open-source assets for enterprise-wide adoption. Evaluate emerging AI/ML techniques, benchmark performance, and validate business impact using real Visa datasets and use cases. Support the end-to-end delivery of AI COE projects, including: Identifying and refining problem statements with stakeholders Prototyping advanced models, pipelines, and automation workflows Building high-quality, reusable code assets Ensuring production readiness and integration with enterprise systems Develop technical documentation, metadata, and best practices for validated AI methods. Contribute to quality assurance through code reviews, prompt engineering support, model evaluation frameworks, and benchmark design. Ensure compliance with governance, security, and Responsible AI standards in all AI COE outputs. Quantify and communicate impact using KPIs such as model accuracy, workflow efficiency gains, adoption metrics, and business value delivered. Collaborate with data scientists, ML engineers, product teams, and global partners to embed AI COE solutions into enterprise workflows and maximize adoption. Stay current on the latest AI frameworks, agentic AI patterns, and LLM ecosystems, rapidly evaluating and prototyping new methods for potential enterprise use. This is a hybrid position.
